title: Algebraic Kunneth formula for tensor products of complexes
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. A cochain complex of $k$-vector spaces is a family of $k$-vector spaces $A^p$ ($p\in\mathbf Z$) with $k$-linear maps $d_A^p:A^p\to A^{p+1}$ and $d_A^{p+1}d_A^p=0$; it is bounded below if $A^p=0$ for all $p$ below some integer. Put $Z^p(A)=\ker(d_A^p)$, $B^p(A)=\operatorname{im}(d_A^{p-1})$ and $H^p(A)=Z^p(A)/B^p(A)$, and similarly for $B$. For two bounded-below complexes $A$ and $B$, form the total tensor-product complex with $(A\otimes_k B)^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}A^p\otimes_k B^q$ and differential $d_A\otimes 1+(-1)^p\,1\otimes d_B$ on $A^p\otimes_k B^q$. For every integer $n$, the map $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^p(A)\otimes_k H^q(B)\to H^n(A\otimes_k B)$, sending $[a]\otimes[b]$ to $[a\otimes b]$, is well defined and is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply lem-sc-tensor-homology-pairing in each bidegree p+q=n. These pairings are proved over any commutative ring; they supply cycle representatives and the correct homology class equation. TensorProduct.lift turns the bilinear pairings into linear maps, and DirectSum.toModule assembles them into the linear map f.
The inclusion iCycles is injective. Hence any cycle z with the specified inclusion equals the supplied representative. This proves the representative equation for f for every such z.

Apply lem-sc-tensor-homology-map-bijective to f and the given bounded-below hypotheses. Convert f into a linear equivalence using LinearEquiv.ofBijective. Its underlying function is f, so the representative equation gives precisely the conclusion of tensor_kunneth.
